findings.title: add_lane understates its destructive behavior
findings.why_it_matters: MCP clients receive destructiveHint: false, whose installed SDK contract says the tool performs only additive updates. add_lane can remove existing flow-node memberships from other lanes and replace persisted pool, lane, node, and connection geometry, so approval UX and policy routing can treat a destructive diagram rewrite as a safe addition.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a destructive non-idempotent annotation tuple (readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false, openWorldHint false), assign it to add_lane, and add a behavior test that moves an already assigned node and verifies both the old membership removal and advertised tuple.
evidence: node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/spec.types.d.ts:1109-1116 defines destructiveHint false as performing only additive updates.
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:600-605 explicitly removes supplied flowNodeIds from every existing lane before adding the new lane.
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:619 and 1377-1427 relayout existing lanes, pool dimensions, flow-node coordinates, connection waypoints, and boundary events as part of add_lane.
tests/contracts/tool-annotations.test.ts:65 locks add_lane to ADDITIVE but has no behavioral probe for moving an existing lane assignment.

residual_risks: scripts/package-smoke.mjs now verifies annotations from live tools/list responses for the source executable, optional bundle, and installed packed executable, but that mutating clean/build/pack workflow was not executed under this review's read-only constraint.
testing_gaps: No annotation contract test exercises add_lane with a flow node already assigned to another lane, the branch that makes the tool destructive rather than purely additive.
